standard.title: Fair play and ethical behaviour
standard.description: demonstrate fair play and reflect on how ethical behaviour can influence physical activity outcomes for individuals and groups
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can transfer and adapt skills from previous experiences to create successful outcomes in unfamiliar situations (AC9HP10M07), and have previously investigated modifications to equipment and rules supporting fair play and inclusion (AC9HP8M08). At Y9-10 the focus extends to reflecting on how ethical behaviour influences outcomes — including contested issues like performance-enhancing drugs.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students demonstrate fair play and reflect on how ethical behaviour influences physical activity outcomes for individuals and groups, including engagement with contested ethical questions in sport.

nodes.label: Fair play in practice
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can demonstrate fair play and analyse how equitable participation influences physical activity outcomes
nodes.minimum_width: Demonstrate fair play in a physical activity context; identify one way equitable participation influenced the outcome for the group
nodes.typical_width: Demonstrate fair play across a range of physical activity contexts; analyse how equitable participation in group activities influences outcomes; analyse how First Nations Australian athletes have been treated in different sports and evaluate the impact on young First Nations Australians' participation
wider: Analyse a specific case of inequitable treatment in sport — evaluate what the impact was on participation, identity and outcomes for those affected, and for the broader sporting community
Investigate how First Nations Australian athletes have navigated inequitable treatment in sport — evaluate how their responses modelled ethical behaviour and influenced cultural change
Evaluate how equitable participation rules in a modified game affect the quality of the experience for all participants — redesign one element to improve equity and evaluate the impact

response_modes.reason: Fair play operates differently across individual sport, team sport, recreational activity, and elite competition contexts. Students who only demonstrate fair play in one familiar context develop a narrow understanding. The First Nations athlete direction is not optional — it addresses a substantive and historically significant dimension of fair play in Australian sport.

success_criteria: Demonstrates at least one specific fair play behaviour during a physical activity
Identifies how equitable participation influenced the outcome — for themselves or others
Does not conflate rule-following with fair play — recognises that fair play includes spirit and intent

nodes.label: Ethical behaviour and sporting outcomes
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can reflect on how ethical behaviour influences physical activity outcomes for individuals and groups, including engagement with contested ethical issues
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one contested ethical issue in sport and reflect on how different positions on it could influence outcomes for individuals and groups
nodes.typical_width: Investigate the use of performance-enhancing drugs in sport and analyse tensions between competing positions on whether they should be permitted; discuss the role of organisations (Sports Integrity Australia, sporting tribunals, Australian Human Rights Commission, Court of Arbitration for Sport) in promoting fairness and ethical behaviour; reflect on how ethical behaviour influences both individual and group outcomes
wider: Construct an evidence-based argument for one position on performance-enhancing drugs in sport — evaluate the strongest counterargument and address it
Investigate the role of Sports Integrity Australia or a specific sporting tribunal in a named case — evaluate how the resolution influenced ethical behaviour standards in that sport
Reflect on a personal experience where ethical or unethical behaviour influenced an outcome — evaluate what the experience revealed about the relationship between integrity and performance

response_modes.reason: Students commonly express strong opinions about ethical issues in sport (PEDs, racism, unfair treatment) without engaging the complexity — taking a position without analysing competing perspectives or evaluating evidence. The structured reasoning investment is in developing the capacity to hold and examine multiple positions simultaneously before reaching a reflective conclusion about how ethics influences outcomes.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Evidence-based argument construction on PEDs, institutional case investigation, and personal reflection on integrity each develop different dimensions of ethical reasoning in sport. Students who engage the wider tier move from describing what ethical behaviour looks like to genuinely reasoning about how and why it influences outcomes at individual, group and institutional levels.
success_criteria: Identifies a specific ethical issue and at least two competing positions on it
Reflects on how different ethical positions influence outcomes — not just which position is correct
Reasoning engages with evidence or principle — not only personal preference
